claims.text: A high-purity alumina (Al2O3) ceramic coating can protect steel-based dipping and plating equipment from molten-aluminum erosion.
The alumina coating will form a stable, chemically inert barrier.
The coating will minimize direct contact between molten aluminum and the steel base metal.
Minimizing contact between molten aluminum and the base metal will reduce erosion.
Unprotected steel or similar metallic substrates undergo rapid erosion in high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The proposed intervention is to apply a high-purity alumina coating to sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates that contact molten aluminum.
The relevant molten-aluminum exposure temperature is approximately 660–700 °C.
The coated parts will undergo repeated thermal and mechanical stresses during dipping service.
A continuous and adherent alumina layer can isolate the underlying metal from molten aluminum.
Alumina has a high melting point.
Alumina is chemically inert with respect to molten aluminum under the stated conditions.
Alumina's stable ceramic structure resists dissolution in molten aluminum.
The alumina barrier limits interfacial reactions that cause erosion and thereby preserves the underlying metal.
Alumina-coated components will have a significantly lower corrosion and erosion rate than uncoated components.
Reducing corrosion and erosion will extend component service life under operational conditions.
Coating adhesion, thermal-expansion mismatch, and mechanical wear may limit long-term protective effectiveness.
